q_exclusive_possession.text: Is exclusive possession of the premises granted to the grantee — the right to exclude all others, including the grantor?
q_exclusive_possession.legal_test: Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor, AIR 1959 SC 1262: exclusive possession is the decisive test. In Maharashtra the distinction is doubly load-bearing because lease (Art 36, ad valorem on a %-of-market-value) and leave & licence (Art 36A, 0.25% of rent+deposit+interest) are SEPARATE articles with very different duty.

q_interest.text: Is the grant intended to create an interest in the property (a term/periodic tenancy, heritable/transferable), rather than a purely personal permission?
q_interest.legal_test: Section 105, Transfer of Property Act 1882; and Maharashtra Rent Control Act context — intention to create an interest confirms a lease (Art 36).

q_indicia.text: Despite a 'leave & licence' label, are there exclusive-possession indicia (grantor excluded, grantee controls access, long fixed term, permanent structures permitted)?
q_indicia.legal_test: Substance over form (Associated Hotels). A licence with exclusive-possession indicia may in substance be a lease chargeable under Art 36, not Art 36A.

grey.reason: Exclusive-possession indicia conflict with the licence label (or intention to create an interest is unclear). Apply s.6 (highest of the competing duties — here Art 36 lease typically exceeds Art 36A) and recommend adjudication (s.31) rather than guessing between two separate Maharashtra articles.

source.ref: Transfer of Property Act 1882 s.105; Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor, AIR 1959 SC 1262; Maharashtra Stamp Act 1958 Arts 36 & 36A, s.6
source.quoted_text: Lease (transfer of exclusive possession creating an interest) is charged under Art 36; leave & licence (bare permission to occupy) under Art 36A. Where indicia conflict, s.6 charges the highest of the competing duties.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the legal tests. Unlike Delhi/Karnataka (which have no separate L&L article), Maharashtra's Art 36 vs 36A split makes this classification directly duty-determinative — the escalation on grey-zone indicia matters most here.
